Diagnosis: `parse_unquoted_value` (parser.py:123-125) reads the rest of the line and strips comments with `re.sub(r"\s+#.*", "", part).rstrip()`. For `KEY= # explanation`, `_equal_sign` (`=[^\S\r\n]*`) already eats the space after `=`, so `part` is `"# explanation"` — no whitespace precedes `#`, so nothing is stripped and the value wrongly becomes `"# explanation"` instead of `""`. `KEY=#literal`/`KEY=a#b` stay literal (correct), and quoted values bypass this path.

Plan: in `parse_unquoted_value`, also treat a leading `#` as a comment, e.g. `re.sub(r"(?:^|\s+)#.*", "", part).rstrip()`, so `KEY= # c` → `""` while `KEY=#literal` → `"#literal"` and `KEY=a#b` → `"a#b"`. Quoting, exports, and ordinary comments are untouched. Add tests for these three cases and re-run the suite.
